conv.notes:
All 17 failing tests in packages/kernel/tests/value-diagnostic-work.test.ts are converted. The other 3 tests in the file (the UTF-16 preflight ones) are unchanged. The file passed 20/20 with node --test --experimental-strip-types on three consecutive runs, about 5 s each. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exited 0 for the whole repository. No other file was edited, and nothing under packages/kernel/src.

**C1 ablation, run and verified.** Every mutant's `before` text was checked to occur exactly once in B (`git show b9c1e549:<path>`) and in the current file. Ablation ran in scratch copies, never in the shared tree:
- B side: `git archive` of B's packages/kernel, with the original test file.
- C side: a copy of the current packages/kernel, with the converted test file.
- Both copies use a symlink to the repo's node_modules.

For each (test, mutant) pair, the mutant was applied, only that test was run (`--test-name-pattern` with the exact title), and the source was restored. Result: 43 pairs at B with the original tests and 43 pairs at C with the converted tests. All 86 were killed and none survived.
- Mutant ids: MD1–MD4, MD6–MD8, MV1–MV3, MB1–MB2, MO1–MO2, MC1, MR1.
- MD8 (the catch label describes the container instead of the thrown value) does not kill the thrown-object deep-chain test at B or at C, because both labels are "object". It is claimed only for the thrown-null/arrays test, where it is killed.
- Runner and results are in the session scratchpad, under tools/ (mutants.py, ablate.py) with ablation.log and ablation-results.json.

**Instrument features implemented locally in the test file. capture-instruments.ts is untouched.**
- A CHILD probe library (a string prepended to each `inWrappedChild` body):
  - Per-target hook routing: Maps keyed by tracked object for descriptor, names, symbols and prototype, since the prelude exposes only one global hook per operation.
  - `fixture`: the Proxy-free twin of the foreign / foreign-array / thrown-object fixtures.
  - `rowFixture`: the twin of the decision-03/04 4,096-position rows. It counts prototypes, both listings, length descriptors and per-position descriptors, with an `unexpected` key counter.
  - `deepAnswer`: hands the Kernel decision-03's prebuilt deep-prototype descriptors directly through the wrapped descriptor primordial.
  - `disagreeingLength`: the length witness.
  - The harness and assertOnlyRefusal, imported inside the child.
- `tripwireFunction`: a plain function whose 13 diagnostic keys, own and inherited, are throwing counting getters.
- `handlerFixture`: puts all 13 trap names behind counting getters at the end of the handler chain, so the witness proves no trap lookup, not just no trap call. `countingProxy` cannot express a deep handler chain.

**Weakening disclosure (rule D).** An ordinary [[Get]] of own data on a plain object runs no caller code and cannot be wrapped. So the original `reads` and `lengthReads` counts cannot survive as counts. They are replaced by disagreement witnesses:
- Read witness: the own descriptor says one value and the element holds another, so every read position is refused, and a skipped read would capture the descriptor's value instead.
- Length witness: the own `length` descriptor says 4,095 while the read says 4,096.
- In the byte-stop tests, the replacement is the meter's element units: 61,471, which pins the positions examined, each element unit being one descriptor plus one read.

These witnesses kill MV1 and MV2, which the original count assertions killed. All other counts stay exact, and the meter values were derived from the unit table and the shape before any run.

**Proxy witnesses.** Each converted test keeps its original Proxy as a W witness, now refused with zero trap calls. That includes the eight-root Outcome and creation/ingress/recovery paths, with the same whole-state facts as before (classification, executionId null, position 0, retry position 1, assertOnlyRefusal, no deliveries).

**Renames (rule D).** The six decision-03/04 tests now carry "(item 5 superseded by decision-01 item 2)". The unsupported-primitive test's meaning changed and it was renamed. Each renamed test quotes its original title in its one-line "K1.1-correction-03: converted from …" comment, and every converted test has that comment.

No production change is needed.

conv.notes:
All 26 failing tests in packages/kernel/tests/values.test.ts are converted. The file now passes 84/84 with `node --test --experimental-strip-types`. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exited 0 with no errors anywhere when last run. I edited only values.test.ts; the other modified files in the checkout belong to concurrent agents. No production code, capture-instruments.ts, harness.ts or records were touched.

C1 ablation:
- Coverage: 48 (test, mutant) pairs across all 26 converted tests. Each mutant's at_b text occurs exactly once in `git show b9c1e549:packages/kernel/src/values.ts`, and each at_c text exactly once in the current values.ts (checked by script).
- Method: ran in isolated `git archive` copies of B and HEAD under the scratchpad, never in the shared checkout. For every pair, the B copy with the at_b mutant ran the ORIGINAL test, and the C copy (HEAD plus my final values.test.ts) with the at_c mutant ran the CONVERTED test, each selected by `--test-name-pattern`.
- Result: every mutant was KILLED on both sides, and all 52 unmutated baselines passed.
- Every mutated values.ts still loads at B and at C, so no kill comes from a syntax error.
- Every C-side kill is an assertion failure (`testCodeFailure`), not a crash or timeout. Two B-side kills (COST-array-structure-charge-dropped and COST-string-bytes-uncharged) happened through the original child's 60 s timeout, which the original test relied on. At C the same mutants are killed by exact issue and meter assertions (`too_much_work` instead of the byte stop).
- Evidence is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-arrokothi/277b30fa-4b8a-523f-b51a-f2df3201c4ce/scratchpad/mut/ (mutants.py, plan.py, ablate.py, results.json, ablate-final.log, reasons-C.json, syntax.py).

Mutants with shared before-text:
- VAL-array-read-from-descriptor and VAL-object-read-from-descriptor share one at_b. B had a single read in describedValue; C splits it into observeElement and captureObject.
- VAL-snapshot-is-caller-object and VAL-snapshot-rereads-caller share one at_c before-text (the finishObject call) with different afters. At C, finishObject has no access to the caller object, so the re-read mutant is placed at its call site. Both mutants bind {"a":2,"b":{}} at C.

How the conversions were done:
- W cases: the original Proxy is kept as a countingProxy witness. Each asserts the exact refusal (unsupported_form, its path, PROXY_MESSAGE) and calls() === 0. Where the Proxy had a side effect, the test also asserts the side effect never ran.
- Defensive capture paths: reached by inWrappedChild hooks on a tracked genuine array or plain object (descriptor, names or prototype hooks that answer differently or throw). The one exception is the hollow-array case, which uses an in-process inherited Array.prototype['0'] instead.
- Serializer-window vectors with no existing twin (Object.keys one-shot, Object.keys throwing, Array.prototype.join): converted to pre-call twins and renamed, keeping "K11-R2-VAL-02 round 6" in the title.
- Capture-time vectors that already had a pre-call twin in the file (toJSON, chain insertion), plus K11-R5-VAL-03 and K11-R6-VAL-04: these use a wrapped-child hook on the Kernel's own observation, so the installation stays capture-time and does not duplicate the twin.
- Every converted test has a "K1.1-correction-03: converted from …" comment. Renamed tests also name their original title.

Strengthening and invariants:
- The three timing gates (`ms < 20_000`) are removed. Exact meter work records and wrapped-primordial counts replace them.
- Upper bounds became exact counts, derived from the value's shape and the unit table, never copied from a run: leaf visits, 16 and 6 element observations, 4,097 descriptor observations, and 0 index descriptors where the originals had < 10 and < 100. The original bounds are still asserted alongside.
- Q1: none of these cost tests reaches the meter stop at C. All still end at the byte stop, and no accepted value changed.
- KC3-9 authority for this file: owner decision-01 item 2 only. There are no item 3 (built-in) or Q4 changes here.

Same-tick vector. I checked the order in coordinator.ts:
- Creation observes scope, creationKey, the three revisions, authorityContext and the initialInput field. Then it captures authorityContext, then observes initialInput kind/payload/subscriptionClass, then captures payload, then commits.
- Ingress observes destination, requestKey, kind, payload and subscriptionClass, then captures payload, then commits.
So an own `payload` getter on the input envelope runs inside the call, before the payload capture, serializer window and commit. An `authorityContext` getter on the request runs before any initial-input field is observed.

The getter installs the pollution before capture rather than mid-capture. For values.ts and the coordinator this is equivalent, because both use only load-time references and the window still runs after the pollution. Each converted test also keeps a countingProxy W witness: refused with the exact reason, `boundaryValueIssues` giving the Proxy message, `calls() === 0`, the side effect never installed, and nothing created or queued.
